title: WhatsApp API Pricing: What Business Need to Know in 2026
snippet:
Firstly, businesses need to obtain WhatsApp API access. Because APIs do not have interfaces, businesses need to integrate them with a messaging software known as a [Business Solution Provider (BSP)](https://respond.io/blog/whatsapp-partners-whatsapp-business-solution-provider) to send and receive messages.
Some BSPs charge WhatsApp API connection fees and per number charges while others like respond.io have no additional costs on top of the subscription. All messaging software comes with a monthly subscription fee.

As mentioned earlier, the charges BSPs impose vary. A majority of them impose additional fees on top of the WhatsApp conversation charges like markups per message or setup fees. While costs differ from one BSP to another, we’ll cover some of the main BSPs in the market and their pricing models.
### SleekFlow WhatsApp API Pricing: WhatsApp Account
Some businesses need to operate multiple WhatsApp accounts—whether to support different branches worldwide, serve distinct teams, or work around the limitations of a single account. If that’s your case, keep in mind that some BSPs, like SleekFlow, charge extra for each additional WhatsApp number.
Specifically, [SleekFlow charges US$15 per month](https://respond.io/sleekflow-alternative) per additional WhatsApp Business phone number.

### Respond.io WhatsApp Business API: Free WhatsApp API Access
Respond.io is a recognized WhatsApp Business Solution Provider (BSP) and customer conversation platform. It allows you to get free WhatsApp API access, manage your WhatsApp Business Account and receive messages in an [omnichannel inbox](https://respond.io/blog/omnichannel-communication).

With respond.io, businesses only need to pay WhatsApp per-message charges that are made compulsory by WhatsApp. It does not impose any additional setup or per-message fees.

If you're looking for a WhatsApp BSP that also offers an AI-powered customer conversation platform, [sign up for respond.io](https://app.respond.io/settings/channels/connectChannel/whatsapp_business) and get free WhatsApp API access.

No. Using WhatsApp Business API involves the following costs:
1. Messaging software costs
2. WhatsApp conversation charges
3. Business Solution Provider fees

title: How to Get WhatsApp API Access: 3 Paths Compared
snippet:
| You need | Why | Watch out for |
|---|---|---|
| A Facebook account or managed Meta account | To sign in to Meta's tools | Use an account tied to the company, not one person's throwaway |
| A Meta business portfolio | Holds your WhatsApp assets and your verification | Note who is admin; only admins can verify or delete numbers |
| A phone number | The identity customers see | It must take an SMS or voice call, have a country and area code, and not be active on WhatsApp |
| A display name | Shown on your WhatsApp profile | It has to match your real brand or it gets rejected |
| A payment method or partner credit line | Paid messages need billing on the Messaging account | Since October 1, 2026, without one, service messages stop once the 1,000 free per month are used |
| Business verification (optional at first) | Raises your limits and number cap | Not needed for a first test, needed to grow past 250 business-initiated recipients a day |
The number is where most projects stall: one already running WhatsApp or the WhatsApp Business app can't be registered until that account is deleted, unless you onboard through a partner that supports coexistence.

## Path 1: Go direct through Meta for Developers
You build against the Cloud API yourself and pay Meta's per-message rates with nothing on top.
1. Register as a developer at developers.facebook.com and create an app with the **Connect with customers through WhatsApp** use case.
2. Pick or create a business portfolio. Meta creates a test WhatsApp account, Messaging account and test phone number for you.
3. In **API Setup**, generate a temporary token and send yourself a test message.
4. Add your real number, verify it with an SMS or voice code, then register it with a call to the `register` endpoint.
5. Create a system user and a long-lived token, add a payment method, and point webhooks at your server.

## Path 2: Sign up through a Business Solution Provider
A Business Solution Provider (BSP, which Meta now calls a Solution Partner) gives you a hosted platform on top of the Cloud API. You usually click a signup link the provider sends, log in with Facebook, choose your business portfolio, verify your number and accept Meta's terms. The provider handles the rest.
Solution Partners have a credit line with Meta, so they can skip the payment-method step and invoice you directly for messages plus their own fees. In return you get an inbox, template tools, chatbots and a support team that knows the platform.

title: WhatsApp Business API Guide 2026: Access, Pricing, Rules
snippet:
The WhatsApp Business API is Meta's Cloud API: your software sends and receives WhatsApp messages through it. You can connect directly through a Meta developer app or through a Business Solution Provider, using a number that can receive a verification code. Meta bills per delivered message by category and country, users' messages are free, and from October 1, 2026 each number gets 1,000 free service messages a month. Business-initiated messages need approved templates and opt-in.
**The WhatsApp Business API is Meta's Cloud API, the programmatic side of the WhatsApp Business Platform that lets software send and receive WhatsApp messages.** You can connect to it directly from a Meta developer app for free or through a Business Solution Provider, and Meta bills per delivered message by category and country.

| Route | Cost | Pick it if | Trade-off |
|---|---|---|---|
| WhatsApp Business app | Free phone app | One person or a small team replying by hand | No API; automation limited to quick replies and away messages |
| Cloud API, direct | Meta charges per message | You have a developer or use n8n and want no platform fee | You build the inbox, logic and template management yourself |
| Cloud API through a BSP | Meta charges plus the provider's fee | You want an inbox, campaigns and support out of the box | Platform fees and less control over data and logic |

Going direct is free to set up and gives you full control. You create a Meta developer app, add the WhatsApp product, connect it to your business portfolio and get a test number to send your first message within minutes. Production needs your own number, an approved display name and, to raise limits, business verification.
A Business Solution Provider, or BSP, does the same onboarding through Meta's embedded signup and gives you a shared inbox, broadcast tools and support. You pay Meta's message charges plus the provider's fee. Most BSP marketing pages blur this line: the provider does not give you different WhatsApp rules or cheaper Meta rates, it gives you software and service.

- **It cannot sit on the consumer app.** A number active on regular WhatsApp has to be removed from it first.

title: WhatsApp Business API in 2026: how it works, what it costs, and how to get access
snippet:
The cost changed on October 1, 2026. Service replies (your answers inside the 24-hour window after a customer writes) are charged again after 1,000 free per phone number per month, at `$0.0034` each in the US and `$0.055` in Germany. Templates you send outside that window are billed from the first message.
The part most guides skip: the API is plumbing, not an app. It has no inbox, no reply logic and no handoff. You still need something on top, a helpdesk, a partner platform, or an AI teammate like [eesel](https://www.eesel.ai/integrations/whatsapp), which answers WhatsApp chats from your help center for 1 credit per conversation and passes refunds and edge cases to your team.

| | WhatsApp Business app | WhatsApp Business API (Cloud API) |
|---|---|---|
| Who uses it | People, on a phone or linked devices | Your software, through a partner or your own code |
| Cost to Meta | Messages sent from the app are free ([Meta](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/embedded-signup/onboarding-business-app-users)) | Billed per delivered message by category and country |
| Automation and AI | Built-in greeting, away messages and quick replies | Anything you build or connect, from rules to AI agents |
| Messages after 24h of silence | Normal chat | Approved templates only |
| Throughput | Not published | 80 messages per second per number, up to 1,000 ([Meta](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/throughput)) |
| Helpdesk connection | None | [Zendesk](https://www.eesel.ai/blog/zendesk-whatsapp-integration), [Freshdesk](https://www.eesel.ai/blog/whatsapp-business-integration-for-freshdesk), [Gorgias](https://www.eesel.ai/blog/gorgias-whatsapp) and others |

1. **Go direct with Meta.** You create the app, host the webhook server and write the code. Meta bills your card.
2. **Use a Solution Partner** (what most people still call a BSP). Meta's [partners overview](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/solution-providers/overview) says Solution Partners have credit lines and can invoice you for API usage, so you may never enter a payment method with Meta.
3. **Use a Tech Provider.** Same full range of services, but no credit line: you add your own card, Meta bills you for messages, and the provider bills you only for its software. Most onboard you with Embedded Signup, a pop-up that creates your WhatsApp assets in a few clicks.

title: How to Apply for WhatsApp Business API Access
snippet:
**Quick answer:** There is no application queue. Create a Meta business portfolio, a WhatsApp account and a Messaging account (the old WABA, split from 23 September 2026), register a number via the API, make a system-user token, verify a webhook and get a template approved (up to 24 hours). You start at 250 unique users a day.

### 3. Choose your route: direct Cloud API, Tech Provider or Solution Partner
**First action:** decide who owns the app that calls the API. Direct, you create a Meta app with the “Connect with customers through WhatsApp” use case, and Meta’s [permissions page](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/permissions/) says a direct developer using only its own data does “not need to undergo App Review”. Through a partner you complete Embedded Signup, which Meta says lets clients “start sending messages in less than five minutes”, and you own the assets it creates. Numbers no longer migrate between Solution Partners; you share your WhatsApp account instead, with up to five Solution Partners. **Finished when:** your app is connected to a Messaging account in API Setup, or your partner has your account and phone number IDs.

The exception is coexistence: a Solution Partner or Tech Provider can [onboard a WhatsApp Business app number](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/embedded-signup/onboarding-business-app-users/) so app and API run side by side, on app version 2.24.17 or later at a fixed 20 messages per second.

**First action:** add your production number in API Setup, which Meta says “generates a WhatsApp account containing that number, along with a Messaging account for your templates and billing” (Meta Business Suite can also create each one). New business portfolios start capped at 2 registered numbers and 250 templates per Messaging account. Verification, or reaching the 2,000 messaging limit, raises the number cap to 20; verification plus an approved display name raises the template cap to 6,000. Add a payment method: Meta’s [pricing page](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/pricing/) says that without one, service messages stop after the free 1,000 per number per month. **Finished when:** both account IDs and a payment method show.
